primary_records_reviewed: The original 115-page Google liability opinion, downloaded from the Justice Department. Relevant text included the opening disposition, header bidding and Last Look at pp. 33–35, the analysis at p. 99 and the separation of procompetitive benefits from challenged preferences at pp. 107–109. Page 35 was rendered and visually inspected; exhaustive reading of all 115 pages is not claimed.

Google's own 19 September 2025 response: integration and separation-cost arguments, predicted effects on small businesses and its proposed interoperability approach. The company's characterization of the acquisitions is not substituted for the court's bounded findings.

The 2 September 2026 remedies opinion as reproduced by FindLaw: judicial text on the rejection of structural remedies, interoperability with Prebid and rival servers, data export and oversight, rather than an editorial headnote. The Justice Department's 16 September announcement was also reviewed. Neither is an implementation audit or proof of final resolution of later proceedings.

Ofwat's detailed P30 case explanation: commencement and dividend principles, the October 2023 payment, distinct March 2024 components, no net cash outflow in the tax-loss arrangement, value effects and future price-control treatment.
Ofwat's household billing-agent explanation: household inability to switch the licensed local provider, without generalizing to every business retail user.

Ofwat's 28 May 2025 final-decision announcement: two separate penalty amounts, wastewater findings and remediation order. Thames Water's own response was read separately, including the company's funding position and the distinct Environment Agency investigation.

Ofwat's 27 August 2025 payment-plan announcement and rationale: twenty-per-cent first instalment and earliest-of-three triggers for the balance. Payment requirements are not reported as verified receipts.
access_limits: Direct access to Ofwat's pages and detailed decision PDFs returned 403. Substantive indexed text of the official case explanation and announcements was available through the search provider and was read, including the full cash/value explanation and payment triggers. The detailed wastewater and dividend decision PDFs were located but not represented as downloaded, independently rendered or exhaustively reviewed.

The Google remedies opinion was read as court text reproduced by FindLaw, not as a locally downloaded original court PDF. Its 2 September date was checked against the reproduced opinion; the later Justice Department announcement is a separate source.

The Google narrative stops with the September 2026 opinions and explanation; the Thames narrative stops with the August 2025 payment plan. Subsequent appeals, judgment text, financing, receipts, implementation and market effects remain outside the articles' stated scope.
